title: Incremental canary + backfill playbook for verified model signatures and pinning
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create an operational playbook and automated tooling to safely canary new Redwood-verified performance signatures and backfill performance profiles for previously onboarded model versions. The playbook will define telemetry gates, automated backfill jobs, pin semantics, and rollback criteria so that engineering and ops teams can publish verified profiles with minimal manual coordination.
background: We publish verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) alongside model artifacts so customers can make predictable routing and cost decisions. Current publish flow is largely manual for canaries and lacks a standard for backfilling older model versions when new kernel/runtime optimizations change performance characteristics. This creates risk of stale profiles, incorrect routing, or customer-facing regressions when runtime upgrades are applied.
goals: Define deterministic canary gates (telemetry, error budgets, perf regressions) for new verified signatures
Automate backfill jobs to recompute profiles for historical model versions after runtime changes
Standardize pin semantics that map model-version -> signed-profile artifact and a safe roll-forward/rollback process
out_of_scope: Full redesign of the profiler agents (ENG work) - we assume existing profiler outputs are unchanged
Customer-facing UI polishing in Console; this ticket focuses on ops/playbook and automation hooks
success_metrics: Reduce manual verification steps for profile publish by 60%
Automated backfill completes for 90% of historical models within SLA after a runtime release
<1% customer-facing routing incidents attributable to stale profiles over the next quarter
acceptance_criteria: A published playbook doc accessible from the onboarding runbook describing gates, thresholds, and roles
A running pipeline that can enqueue and execute profile backfills with idempotency and status tracking
Canary automation that runs against N (configurable) replicas and emits pass/fail signals into the publish pipeline
Signed profile artifact format documented and tooling to pin/unpin artifacts with audit log entries
risks: Backfill compute cost could spike if naive full-refresh is used; need incremental strategies
False positives in canary telemetry could block releases unnecessarily
Rollbacks of pinned profiles require coordination with Dedicated/Private customers who may have pinned versions
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Draft playbook + telemetry gates and review with ENG/Runtime/Console (two-week review)
Phase 2: Prototype canary runner that executes profile generation on a small replica fleet; collect metrics
Phase 3: Implement backfill queue worker with rate limits and cost guardrails; run against a 30-day model subset
Phase 4: Integrate artifact signing and pin/unpin APIs; publish playbook and training session for oncall
Phase 5: Gradual enablement for all model families with monitoring dashboards and alerts
telemetry_thresholds: Latency P95 delta <= 7% compared to baseline in canary windows
Token generation error-rate increase <= 0.3 percentage points
Throughput variance within +/-10% for steady-state traffic
automation_tasks: Backfill queue worker with concurrency control and cost budget annotations
Canary runner that launches profile generation jobs and aggregates metrics into a canary-result artifact
Publish pipeline step that verifies canary-result artifacts and signs published profiles
Audit log hook to record pin/unpin operations and actor identity
manual_checklist: PM/Eng review of telemetry baselines before enabling automated canaries
Security review of signing key rotation schedule
Stakeholder sign-off for default pin-to-profile policy for Hosted vs Dedicated customers
rollback_criteria: Canary indicates >7% P95 regression for two consecutive windows
Observed customer-error-rate increase >0.5 percentage points in production routes using the new profile
Backfill job failure rate above 10% and manual remediation backlog grows
